examInfo.format: 12 Single Choice + 4 Multiple Choice (Prüfungsstil, mit Rechenfragen)
examInfo.grading: Übungsset ohne Note — Ziel: ≥ 60 % der Punkte

questions.text: In MRP II, Material Requirements Planning (MRP) is…

choices.text: step 5 of 5 and is carried out daily
step 4 of 5 and is carried out weekly
step 4 of 6 and is carried out monthly
step 3 of 5 and is carried out annually

questions.explanation: MRP II: 1 Business Planning, 2 S&OP/Aggregated Planning, 3 MPS, 4 MRP, 5 Production Activity Control/Scheduling. MRP ist Schritt 4 und wird wöchentlich gerechnet – nicht jährlich.

questions.text:
A chair consists of 1 seat (CHF 15), 4 legs and assembly work of CHF 8. Each leg costs CHF 5 own cost plus 2 bolts at CHF 0.50 each.

What are the total costs of one chair?
questions.explanation: Bottom-up: Bein = 5 + 2·0.5 = 6. Stuhl = 8 + 15 + 4·6 = 47. Ohne Schrauben: 43; Schrauben nur einmal pro Stuhl statt pro Bein: 44.

questions.text:
MRP: gross requirements of a component in week 6 are 120 units, on-hand inventory is 45 units, scheduled receipts amount to 30 units.

What is the net requirement?

A component is needed in week 7. Its lead time is 3 weeks.

In which week must the planned order be released?
questions.explanation: Offset rückwärts: Bestelldatum = Bedarfsdatum − Lead Time = 7 − 3 = 4. Addieren (Woche 10) ist die klassische Falle.

questions.text:
MRP with lot-for-lot ordering: on-hand at the start is 50 units, lead time 2 weeks, no scheduled receipts. Gross requirements: week 1: 20, week 2: 30, week 3: 40, week 4: 10.

What quantity is released in week 1?
questions.explanation: Bestand: W1 50−20 = 30; W2 30−30 = 0. W3 Netto = 40 ⇒ Release 2 Wochen früher = W1: 40. (W4 Netto 10 ⇒ Release W2: 10.)

questions.text:
The MPS releases 80 bikes in week 5. Each bike needs 2 wheels. 60 wheels are on hand, no receipts are scheduled.

What is the net requirement of wheels in week 5?
questions.explanation: Bruttobedarf des Kindes = 80·2 = 160; Netto = 160 − 60 = 100. Multi-Level-MRP: Release des Elternteils × BOM-Menge = Bruttobedarf des Kindes.

questions.text:
Chase strategy: a month requires 130 units, one worker produces 20 units per month.

How many workers are needed?

Demand per month: 100, 160, 100, 140 units. One worker produces 20 units per month; 5 workers are employed at the start. Wage CHF 2'000 per worker and month, hiring cost CHF 1'000, firing cost CHF 1'500 per worker.

What are the total costs of the chase strategy?
Same data as in the previous question. How many workers does the level strategy employ (constant workforce, no negative inventory)?
questions.explanation: Gesamtbedarf 500 / (4 Monate · 20) = 6.25 ⇒ 7. Mit 6 Mitarbeitern wäre der Lagerbestand in Monat 2 negativ (20 + 120 − 160 = −20).

questions.text:
Three jobs arrive at the same time: A (3 days, due day 8), B (5 days, due day 6), C (1 day, due day 4).

What is the total tardiness under the SPT rule?
questions.explanation: SPT = C, A, B: Completion 1, 4, 9 ⇒ Tardiness 0, 0, max(0, 9−6) = 3. (EDD: Total 1, FCFS A-B-C: Total 7.)

questions.text: Same three jobs. Which priority rule gives the smallest MAXIMUM tardiness?
questions.explanation: EDD (C, B, A): Completion 1, 6, 9 ⇒ Tardiness 0, 0, 1 ⇒ Max 1. SPT hat Max 3, FCFS Max 5. EDD minimiert die maximale Verspätung, SPT die mittlere Durchlaufzeit.

questions.text: A manufacturer wants to assign 4 warehouses to 4 cities (each exactly once) at minimum transport cost using the Excel Solver. Which setup is appropriate?

choices.text: Binary decision variables x_ij, row and column sums equal to 1, Simplex LP
Continuous variable alpha between 0 and 1, GRG Nonlinear
Exponential smoothing with Solver on the MSE

questions.explanation: Zuordnungsproblem = LP mit binären Variablen x_ij ∈ {0,1}; Zeilen- und Spaltensummen = 1; Zielfunktion Σ c_ij·x_ij minimieren (Simplex LP).

sections.title: Part B – Multiple Choice (4 Points)
sections.description: At least two answers are correct. Only the complete correct combination scores (no partial points).

questions.text: Which statements about MRP II are correct?

choices.text: Aggregated Planning determines, for example, how many employees and machines are required.
The steps of MRP II are coordinated and give feedback to each other.
Material Requirements Planning is the third step.
MRP is typically carried out annually.

questions.explanation: 5 Schritte: Business Planning, S&OP/Aggregated, MPS, MRP, Production Activity Control. Schritte sind koordiniert mit Feedback. MRP ist Schritt 4 und wöchentlich.

questions.text: Which statements about Just-in-Time (JIT) are correct?

choices.text: JIT follows the pull principle: actual demand drives production.
The goal of JIT is to produce as fast as possible (Seiso).
Standardisation of processes and products is an important component.
JIT is always superior to planning-based approaches like MRP II.

questions.explanation: JIT = Pull (Kanban), Standardisierung (5S), flexible Mitarbeiter. Ziel ist nicht Geschwindigkeit, sondern Verschwendung vermeiden («genau dann, wenn nötig»). Seiso = Säubern (5S). JIT ist MRP II nicht per se überlegen.

questions.text: Which statements about sequencing (scheduling) rules are correct?

choices.text: No priority rule is superior in all performance measures.
SPT minimises the mean flow time of the jobs.
Sequencing is also relevant in the service sector.
FCFS always leads to the lowest average tardiness.

questions.explanation: SPT: mittlere Durchlaufzeit; EDD: maximale Verspätung; keine Regel dominiert überall; Sequenzplanung gilt auch für Services (Beratung, Praxis). FCFS ist nicht per se besser als SPT/EDD.

questions.text: Which statements about chase and level strategy are correct?

choices.text: The chase strategy adapts the workforce to the demand of every month.
The chase strategy leads to higher hiring and firing costs.
The level strategy has no inventory holding costs.
In the level strategy the inventory must not become negative.
The level strategy uses inventory to absorb demand fluctuations.

questions.explanation: Chase: Belegschaft folgt der Nachfrage ⇒ Einstellungs-/Entlassungskosten. Level: konstante Belegschaft ⇒ Lager (Haltekosten), Bestand darf nicht negativ werden. Level hat also gerade Lagerkosten.
